purpose: Trigger accuracy of the YAML description: does the skill fire when it should, and stay quiet when a neighbouring skill or a plain edit owns the request.
method: Real .claude/skills registration in a scratch git repo, not skill-creator's .claude/commands loop (which measures recall at 0-17% against 3/3 and 12/12 for real registration; see the repo memory note). One variant registered at a time under the real skill name, so the name is not a variable. The user-level copy at ~/.claude/skills/session-cleanup is moved out of the skills tree for the whole run, because a parked copy left in place stays registered under its new directory name and fires instead. Every other installed user-level skill stays available, so the negatives compete against real neighbours. The repo is restored from a pristine copy before every query, because a fired skill deletes branches and files and would otherwise change the setup for the next query.
